quests.question: I forgot my password, so I couldn't _____ in to my account.
quests.explanation: 'Log in' means to enter your account using a username and password.

quests.question: My laptop is _____ than my old one, but it's much lighter.
quests.explanation: 'Than' signals a comparison, and short adjectives like 'fast' add -er: faster than the old one.

quests.question: Please don't share your password _____ anyone.
quests.explanation: We 'share something with someone': share a file with a colleague, share a password with no one.

quests.question: I _____ the app yesterday, and it works well.
quests.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished time, so the past simple is needed.

quests.question: There isn't _____ Wi-Fi in this part of the building.
quests.explanation: Negatives use 'any' with uncountable nouns like Wi-Fi, space or data: there isn't any Wi-Fi.

quests.question: Click the link, and the file _____ automatically.
quests.explanation: A general result uses the present simple, and 'file' takes -s.

quests.question: He spends _____ much time on his phone that he hardly sleeps.
quests.explanation: 'So much... that' shows a result: so much time that he hardly sleeps.

quests.question: Is there a charger I can _____ for an hour?
quests.explanation: 'Borrow' is to take something temporarily; 'lend' is to give it.

quests.question: My phone fell _____ the table and the screen cracked.
quests.explanation: We say 'fall off' a surface; 'off' is the preposition, not 'of'.

quests.question: Switch your phone _____ before the film begins.
quests.explanation: 'Switch off' means to stop a device working; 'switch on' starts it. Both work with phones.

quests.question: The software update will be _____ automatically overnight.
quests.explanation: 'Will be' + past participle forms the future passive: the update will be installed overnight.

quests.question: I think my account has been _____; someone changed my password.
quests.explanation: 'Hacked' means accessed by someone without permission. 'Hooked' and 'hatched' have other meanings.

quests.question: Always _____ up your files so you don't lose important work.
quests.explanation: 'Back up' means to save a copy of your data, so you can recover it if something goes wrong.

quests.question: The website is temporarily _____ due to maintenance.
quests.explanation: 'Unavailable' means can't be accessed; 'unable' describes people.

quests.question: You need a stable internet _____ to join the video call.
quests.explanation: 'Internet connection' is the fixed noun phrase; a video call needs a stable one.

quests.question: The app keeps _____, so I'm going to reinstall it.
quests.explanation: 'Keep' is followed by an -ing form for repeated actions: the app keeps crashing, keeps freezing.

quests.question: Don't click on links in emails from people you don't _____.
quests.explanation: After 'don't' the verb stays in its base form: people you don't know, things you don't need.

quests.question: Your subscription will _____ automatically unless you cancel.
quests.explanation: 'Renew' means to continue a subscription or contract for another period.

quests.question: Please _____ the system before you start the update.
quests.explanation: 'Restart' means to switch a device off and on again, the classic first fix for tech problems.

quests.question: I need to _____ some space on my phone to install the update.
quests.explanation: 'Free up' means to make something available by removing other things.

quests.question: She was _____ to find that the file had been deleted.
quests.explanation: The -ed adjective describes how a person feels: she was annoyed. The -ing form describes the cause.

quests.question: Your phone will beep _____ the battery is low.
quests.explanation: 'When' links the beep to the moment the battery runs low; 'where' refers to a place.

quests.question: Despite _____ warned, many users still reuse the same password.
quests.explanation: 'Despite' is followed by -ing; the passive uses 'being' + participle.

quests.question: The basic plan is free, _____ the premium plan costs ten dollars a month.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two facts in one sentence; 'whereby' means 'by which' and explains a system.

quests.question: The system is _____ to cyberattacks if it isn't updated regularly.
quests.explanation: 'Vulnerable to' means easily harmed by something: vulnerable to attack, to fraud, to errors.

quests.question: Users are _____ to enable two-factor authentication for extra security.
quests.explanation: 'Be urged to' + base verb means strongly encouraged to do something.

quests.question: The algorithm, _____ by researchers in Bengaluru, can detect fraud in seconds.
quests.explanation: A past participle phrase can shorten 'which was developed': 'the tool, developed by researchers'.

quests.question: The firm denies _____ customer data without consent.
quests.explanation: 'Deny' is followed by an -ing form: she denied sharing the data, not 'denied to share'.

quests.question: She _____ have seen the message; her phone was switched off all day.
quests.explanation: 'Can't have' + participle: a strong belief that something was impossible.

quests.question: The outage affected users _____ the region, not only business customers.
quests.explanation: 'Across' + an area means in all parts of it: across the region, across the country.
